reasoning: The first clause is a proposal, as the claim's own basis and horizon say, so creative speculation of that kind is not an error. The because-clause is the defect: 'has already secured' reads an achieved event, and the Mill Compact, Council steward and lineage loyalty are not stated in the cited items (E5 is truncated, so its unseen remainder is not checked). E7 states the Special Draw Right is conditional on training outside apprentices, which a refusal of outside crew would appear to strain. The cited words do not address that.
quote: The Special Draw Right is conditional on training apprentices from outside the lineage.
alternative_reading: No quote was offered. Read as a whole proposal, with the Mill Compact introduced as a new institution rather than recorded, the claim is defensible. The record does not carry 'has already secured' as achieved. E5's 'refuses to be counted' concerns a generation, not a steward refusing crew.
would_settle: A cited item that names a Mill Compact and a Council steward, and states the loyalty outcome as achieved, would settle the because-clause as record.
creative_room: The refusal stays open as a proposal for a later Book, and a steward or Mill Compact may be introduced as new proposals. The stage's question about what the lineage must carry stays open as a creative question. Only the loyalty premise must be treated as proposal, not record. E7's condition on outside apprentices is a usable complication.

clauses.text: A later Book could have the Council steward refuse the outside crew
clauses.note: A proposal, as its own basis and horizon say. No cited item names a Council steward; E7 names outside-lineage apprentices, a different thing.

clauses.text: because the Mill Compact has already secured the lineage's loyalty
clauses.note: Mill Compact, lineage loyalty and a secured outcome are not stated in any cited item. 'Has already secured' reads an achieved event the cited words do not carry.

clauses.text: The stage asks what the lineage would then have to carry.
clauses.note: E1 says lineage crews carry channel repair from Book 20 under the Right. 'Would then have to' depends on the proposed refusal, so it holds only if that does.

clauses.text: The stage asks what it would mean for the labour.
clauses.note: E5 frames the labour gap as first met by people. Asking what it would mean is a stage question that follows from that framing, not a record claim.

defensible_possibility: A later Book in which a Council steward refuses the outside crew, offered as proposal, with the Mill Compact and the lineage's loyalty also proposed rather than recorded. The refusal could strain E7's stated condition as a complication.
